title: Token Theft
overview: Investigate synthetic use of one application session fingerprint from different context and risk signals.
prerequisites: Know the basics of Identity auditing and how to review authorization context.

attack.name: Application Access Token
attack.rationale: Observed reuse can be consistent with application token abuse. It does not establish how the token was obtained.

hypothesis: Successful application session use from an unmanaged context and a new ASN merits a pivot to the original sign-in.
evidence: Compare session identifiers, network and device posture enrichments, then check data or control-plane actions.
false_positive: A legitimate device replacement or roaming user may appear in a new context.
tuning: Combine ASN drift with device confidence and prior sign-in evidence. Avoid treating geography as a sole signal.
response: Verify user activity out of band, revoke suspicious sessions and scope subsequent access.
prevention: Enforce phishing-resistant authentication, managed device policy and token binding where supported.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: This lesson observes possible token reuse. The fingerprint is an inert label and identifies no real token.

questions.explanation: The session, actor and surrounding context support the pivot.

questions.prompt: Which response closes an active session?
options: Revoke sessions using the identity provider
questions.explanation: Session revocation addresses access already established.
